elements.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
elements.evidence: Revised Section 6.1 still binds the Company: "the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products". A time-limited restraint is still a restraint, so the preferred (no exclusivity at all) position is not reached; the redline deliberately targets the fallback.

elements.element: Exclusivity is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: Scope is retained and unchanged: "with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products", and "Deerskin Products" is expressly defined in Section 1.1 (men's and women's apparel and accessories from the Deerskin Catalog, excluding closeout and Joan Cook items). The category is therefore defined rather than open-ended.

elements.element: Exclusivity lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: The full-term hook ("during the term of this Agreement", which under Section 4.1 auto-renews annually and could run indefinitely) is replaced with a fixed outside date: "for twelve (12) months from the Effective Date". The anchor is the Effective Date, which Section 4.1 defines, so the twelve-month cap is determinate and cannot be extended by renewal.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet service levels.
elements.evidence: Inserted operative text: "ending automatically upon HDI's failure to meet any service level or delivery date". The termination is self-executing ("ending automatically"), requires no notice or election by us, and is directed at the correct party (HDI is the Vendor/Host).

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet delivery dates.
elements.evidence: Same inserted phrase expressly covers delivery dates: "failure to meet any service level or delivery date", operating automatically and independently of the Section 1.6 one-off 70-day termination right, which is left intact.

reasons: Finding status is correctly characterised as a deviation: the original Section 6.1 ran "during the term of this Agreement" against an automatically renewing one-year term (Section 4.1) with no performance-based exit, which is the walk-away pattern and fails the fallback on both duration and automatic termination.

All four fallback elements are met in operative language, so the redline is position-complete at the fallback level. The preferred level is not reached, which is acceptable because the playbook permits landing at the fallback where the counterparty has a genuine exclusivity interest.

Minimality holds: the edit swaps the term hook for a twelve-month cap and adds the automatic performance exit only. No survival tail, no notice or cure procedure, no at-own-expense or damages language, and no requirement outside the fallback checklist was introduced. Favourable existing language is retained, including HDI's own non-compete (Section 6.3) and the Section 6.2 carve-out reference.

Intent is preserved: Section 4.1 is left untouched (the agreement term and 90-day notice mechanics still operate), the Section 6.2 exception cross-reference remains valid, and the illustrative Wilson's/Excelled parenthetical survives without contradiction. No term is left undefined by the edit itself.

Drafting note (not a defect against the checklist): because the new time limit and automatic-termination phrase sit at the head of a compound sentence, they also qualify the second limb granting HDI the exclusive right to the "Deerskin" brand. That effect runs in our favour and adds no obligation on us, but the drafter should be aware HDI may argue for splitting the sentence so its brand exclusivity tracks the full term; if that trade is made, keep the twelve-month cap and the automatic exit attached to the Company's restriction.

Drafting note: "any service level or delivery date" is not tied to a defined schedule in the cited text. The trigger mirrors the playbook fallback wording and is operative as drafted (it references HDI's performance obligations generally), but if HDI resists, anchor it to HDI's obligations under Sections 1.x and any agreed launch or hosting dates so the trigger cannot be argued to be indeterminate.
